skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through a disciplined debugging process for bugs, test failures, and unexpected behavior. It emphasizes reproducing issues, tracing root causes, testing one hypothesis at a time, and verifying fixes before moving on.
skill.summary: Apply a four-phase method to find root causes before changing code.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

content.value_statement: Unstructured bug fixing wastes time and can hide the real failure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through evidence-based root cause analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guides a four-phase workflow from reproduction to verified fix.
Prompts careful reading of errors, stack traces, recent changes, and configuration differences.
Encourages tracing bad values backward through callers until the original trigger is found.
Supports pattern comparison against working examples before implementation.
Requires one hypothesis and one minimal test change at a time.
Includes guidance for condition-based waits and defensive validation.
limitations: Does not execute diagnostics or inspect projects on its own.
Does not replace domain knowledge for specialized frameworks or systems.
May slow very small fixes if the cause is already proven.
Example commands are illustrative and require user judgment before use.

use_cases.title: Debug failing tests
use_cases.description: QA engineers can trace intermittent or repeatable test failures without stacking unrelated fixes.

use_cases.title: Investigate production defects
use_cases.description: Backend developers can follow evidence from symptoms through services, data flow, and recent changes.

use_cases.title: Coach AI coding sessions
use_cases.description: Technical leads can make Claude, Codex, or Claude Code explain root cause before proposing patches.

prompt_templates.title: Start a debugging session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic debugging on this issue. First, restate the symptom, reproduction steps, and the evidence you need before proposing any fix.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a test failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the four phases to this failing test. Read the error, identify the failing boundary, form one hypothesis, and suggest the smallest verification step.

prompt_templates.title: Compare working and broken paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a working example near this broken behavior. Compare inputs, configuration, dependencies, and call flow before recommending one targeted change.

prompt_templates.title: Recover from failed fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: I already tried several fixes. Stop implementation, list what each attempt proved, identify assumptions, and propose a root cause investigation plan.

output_examples.input: A test creates a repository in the project root instead of a temporary directory.
output_examples.output: The assistant traces the bad directory value backward, identifies early access to an unset test fixture, and recommends validating the directory source.

output_examples.input: An async test passes locally but fails in CI.
output_examples.output: The assistant flags fixed sleep timing as a weak signal and recommends waiting for a real completion condition.

output_examples.input: Three patches changed symptoms but did not fix the defect.
output_examples.output: The assistant stops further patching, summarizes evidence from each attempt, and asks for architecture-level review before more changes.

best_practices: Reproduce the issue and preserve the exact error before editing files.
Test one hypothesis with the smallest useful change.
Add validation where invalid data first enters the system.
anti_patterns: Applying several fixes before proving the root cause.
Ignoring stack traces because the error looks familiar.
Treating a symptom location as the source of the bug.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when debugging a bug, test failure, regression, or unexpected behavior before changing code.

faq.question: Can it fix code automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide an AI assistant to propose fixes after evidence review, but it does not execute changes by itself.

faq.question: Does it work for flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It favors condition-based evidence and minimal experiments over timing guesses.

faq.question: What makes it different from normal debugging advice?
faq.answer: It enforces a phased process: reproduce, trace, compare, test one hypothesis, and verify the final fix.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Are the command examples safe?
faq.answer: They are documentation examples for local debugging. Review commands in your project context before running them.
